title: The Milky Way Above SOAR on Cerro Pachón
caption: The Milky Way above the SOAR telescope, Cerro Pachón, Chile

recognition.text: Image from an NSF NOIRLab announcement. No published audience rating.

story: The Milky Way's band spans the night sky over the SOAR telescope, which sits on Cerro Pachón, a mountain among the Andean foothills of Chile. Along the horizon, airglow adds vivid colors to the scene.

Airglow is a faint light given off by energized atoms in Earth's upper atmosphere. It is always present, but it is usually too dim to notice by eye, and cameras taking long exposures pick it up as bands of color low in the sky.

Cerro Pachón hosts more than SOAR. Gemini South, which forms half of the NSF NOIRLab-operated International Gemini Observatory, and Vera C. Rubin Observatory also share the summit area. High, dry mountaintops like this one are favoured for telescopes because they offer dark skies and a steady atmosphere, placing instruments above much of the air that blurs starlight.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera on Cerro Pachón, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way and airglow appear brighter and more colorful than they would to someone standing there.
